title: Minimum Lights to Illuminate a Road
summary: Given an array of integers representing positions on a road, where each position can have a working bulb or not, determine the minimum number of additional bulbs needed to ensure every position is illuminated by at least one bulb.
statement: Given an array of integers representing positions on a road, where each position can have a working bulb or not, determine the minimum number of additional bulbs needed to ensure every position is illuminated by at least one bulb. Each additional bulb illuminates positions within a range of one position to either side.
constraints: lights[i]=0 means no working light; a positive value is that light’s illumination radius.
An added bulb has radius one.
Return the fewest added bulbs needed to illuminate every road position.
hints: Mark every position covered by existing variable-radius lights using a difference array.
Uncovered positions form independent runs; one added radius-one bulb covers at most three consecutive positions.
For each uncovered run add ceil(length/3).
Greedily placing bulbs every third position covers a run with exactly that lower-bound number.
editorial: Greedily placing bulbs every third position covers a run with exactly that lower-bound number.

tests.explanation: Two added radius-one bulbs cover all four positions.
The existing center light already covers the road, so return zero.
